messages.author: bfa4a88c8a5bc54e
messages.subject: makePSOCKcluster error with JAGS
parts:
G'day all,

I recently started getting a strange error when running JAGS on my Macbook Pro (macOS Catalina 10.15.5). After I run a model, it runs for a while but then comes up with this:

Processing function input....... 

Done. 
 
Error in makePSOCKcluster(names = spec, ...) : 
  Cluster setup failed. 3 of 3 workers failed to connect


The same script runs fine on a Windows machine and it used to work fine on my own Macbook as well. Google has been pretty unhelpful and I haven't been getting answers on the SourceForge site for JAGS. Does anyone know what's going on?

Kind regards,
Matt

messages.author: 5ff906c2720491d5
messages.subject: Re: makePSOCKcluster error with JAGS
parts:
Hi Matt,

I also started to get this error after I updated my R to the latest version. My pre-update working code started to give this error as well. I use jagsUI package and when  I changed in my ‘jags‘ function “parallel” argument from TRUE to FALSE (“parallel=FALSE“) then the model ran without any problem. After a quick googling my understanding of the problem was the newest update somehow prevents jags to clustering the chains, that’s why the model chains do not run parallel, so when I tell the model not to run parallel then there is no problem. I couldn’t find a solution yet, if you do so I would like to try it out as well.

Best
Dilsad

messages.author: 068cbc8bd5fb0d5d
messages.subject: Re: makePSOCKcluster error with JAGS
parts:
This only happens with RStudio current versions on Mac OS. They are aware of it and are working on it for a future RStudio release but it’s been months without a solution on their end so I wouldn’t wait for that. If you do the final MCMC run in R and not RStudio it will work in parallel. There is a workaround to get the parallel processors working in RStudio that I don’t think has any noticeable slowdown of performance. You can add this to your code or even to your .rprofile
parallel:::setDefaultClusterOptions(setup_strategy = "sequential")
This might break code on a non-Mac OS if you’re a sharing it so the .Rprofile is probably a better place for it as a temporary solution. 

iirc the code just sets up the socketclusters one at a time but then runs the code in parallel. I could be wrong and don’t have a Mac to try on currently. Best to give it a try on a short test run of just a few iterations per chain. 

Hope that helps,
Daniel Hocking

Happy Sunday --- Marc
